note: The styles of the anidoodle engine. A style is a film: film is its export name in canvas-core; folder (optional, from the engines folder) is where a new style's own canvas-core/<film>.ts lives, looked up before the bundled films. size, duration and fps must equal the film's own meta. To add a style, see README.md, Make a new style.

crayon.about: A crayon picture drawn on stroke by stroke, then it comes alive (a hot-air balloon).

cyanotype.about: A cyanotype drafting sheet where a machine is drawn, measured and set going (a train).

paper-collage.about: Cut-paper pieces laid down one by one into a picture (a fox at dusk).

toy-theatre.about: A paper toy theatre with flats that slide and bob, animated on twos (a seaside town).

oil.about: An oil still life painted stroke by stroke (pears and a copper pot).

woodblock.about: A woodblock print pressed one colour block after another (herons on a bridge in rain).

scratchboard.about: White lines scratched out of a black board (a lynx in moonlight).

single-line-engraving.about: One spiral line whose thickness makes the picture, unspooling (a Mellan engraving).

stipple.about: A pen-and-ink picture built from dots (a nautilus shell).

pixel-art.about: A pixel-art scene with a little character action (a cat's pounce).

flat-vector.about: A flat vector illustration whose shapes move together (a sailing regatta).

isometric.about: A cutaway seen from an angle, where a small process runs inside (a night bakery).

coloured-pencil.about: A coloured-pencil drawing with a small story in it (a tin repairman).

pencil-watercolour.about: A pencil drawing that gets its watercolour washes (a ranunculus flower).

risograph.about: A small-press print built up one ink at a time (a lighthouse at sunset).

ink-wash.about: An ink line drawing that washes in its tones (a wren on a twig).

mid-century.about: A 1950s gouache illustration with flat textured colour (a kite).

rubber-hose.about: A 1930s rubber-hose cartoon loop (a dancing coffee pot).

low-poly.about: A flat low-poly picture whose facets shift with the light (a mountain lake at dawn).

broken-colour.about: Impressionist dabs of pure colour side by side that shimmer, like a harbour at sunrise.

charcoal.about: A charcoal drawing that is rubbed out and drawn again, so one picture changes through time (a tree in four seasons).

dream-glaze.about: Soft translucent glazes laid over each other until a dreamy painting appears.

embroidery.about: A picture stitched in thread on linen, stitch by stitch (a wreath and a bee).

folk-tale.about: A folk-tale picture book: a drawn hero walks through a decorated scene (a boy with a rooster).

halftone.about: A picture printed in newspaper dots, with the dots moving as the light changes (a viaduct at golden hour).

scrapbook.about: An old scrapbook page: clippings, engravings and notes taped in to explain a subject (how a honeybee finds flowers).

storybook.about: A children's-book character in pencil and soft watercolour, drawn before your eyes.

toy-brick.about: A scene built from plastic toy bricks with a small action in it (a tug boat).

sumi-e.about: Japanese ink painting with a brush: bamboo bending in the wind.

marker-comic.about: A comic panel drawn with markers, line then colour (koi fish).

chalkboard.about: A lesson written and drawn in chalk on a blackboard (the phases of the moon).

ballpoint.about: A ballpoint-pen sketch drawn line by line (a pocket watch).

own-example.about: The template for a new style: a circle drawn on, then a dot, in FrameMotion's own film file.
